messages:
Alice M.: Anyone else seeing Trivy DB fetches failing and then the scanner queue blowing up? started around 09:12 UTC.
scanner-runner-bot: job 2026-04-06-09:12-tnx-789 FAILED: upstream fetch error (HTTP 429) while downloading vuln DB. retrying with backoff
Bob K.: yup, saw ~30 failed runs in the last hour. looks like GHAS+Snyk + Trivy pulls all hitting the same CDN origin.
Carol R.: also getting intermittent KMS decrypt errors in the worker logs — sometimes the scanner can't decrypt the PK to fetch creds, then it retries and hits rate limits.
Carol R.: log snippet:
```
2026-04-06T09:11:48Z ERROR decrypt: kms.decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:alias/scanner-key
  at scanner/worker/crypto.go:82
  retrying in 1s
```
Bob K.: hmm, KMS + fetch retries -> thundering herd. we need two things: 1) limit concurrent scanner jobs per region, 2) cache vuln DB layers and share across runners.
Dave (Infra): agree. short-term: reduce parallelism to 10 per cluster and add jittered exponential backoff on 429s. Long-term: local registry-sidecar caching for Trivy DB pulls.
Alice M.: any RBAC changes required for KMS? Carol, can you confirm which principal is failing?
Carol R.: failures are from the ephemeral role used by the gitlab-runner pods: arn:aws:sts::111:assumed-role/scanner-role/runner-*. Looks like a policy regression after the role rename last week.
Carol R.: policy diff:
```
- "Action": "kms:Decrypt",
+ "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:alias/scanner-key",
```
Carol R.: the rename dropped the AssumeRole condition that mapped pod serviceaccount -> role. probably why AccessDenied appears.
Bob K.: OK, urgent fix: re-add the IRSA mapping and rotate the role alias back. Also we should fail the scan early if KMS decrypt fails (so we don't hammer the vuln DB).
sec-bot: NOTE: suppression-rule edits are not currently captured in audit logs. Recent PRs show manual suppressions added in Snyk but not mirrored to GHAS.
Alice M.: that's been a recurring pain — suppression drift. Can we add a lightweight audit webhook that records suppression changes to an internal bucket + Slack alert?
Dave (Infra): yes. implement a serverless webhook that writes to S3 and emits a small JSON with who/what/when. also add a periodic reconciliation job to surface mismatches.
Bob K.: for immediate scanner stability:
- throttle scanner concurrency (helm values -> concurrency: 10)
- add token-bucket on DB fetches (burst 5, rate 1/s)
- add local filesystem cache for DB tarballs (ttl 6h)
- fail-fast on KMS decrypt error
Carol R.: i've re-applied the role mapping in staging. will promote to prod after one more verification run.
Alice M.: thanks. follow-ups:
- Dave: deploy concurrency change + token-bucket middleware (ETA 2h)
- Carol: confirm KMS fix in prod and post logs (ETA 30m)
- Bob: prototype S3 audit webhook + reconciliation job (ETA EOD)
- me: update runbook and add a one-line note to the incident channel if we see more 429s :eyes:
Bob K.: also consider pinning Trivy to a vendor image SHA to avoid sudden behavior changes.
Dave (Infra): added helm patch diff in PR #421 (concurrency + backoff config). deploy kicking off.
scanner-runner-bot: job 2026-04-06-11:27-tnx-812 SUCCEEDED (after reduced concurrency)
Alice M.: nice. leaving this thread open until reconciliation job shows no drift. thanks all :thumbsup:
